@P240.context: | 240 | **@P240** — A bounded-generic function whose body computes TWO OR MORE bound-supplied operator results into local variables, then returns them in a tuple constructor, produced wrong values under one backend in a way that depended on whether the body had intervening side-effects (e.g., a `println!`).  Reproducer: `fn classify<T: Ordered>(a: T, b: T) -> (integer, integer) { lt = if a < b { 1 } else { 0 }; gt = if a > b { 1 } else { 0 }; (lt, gt) }` invoked with `classify(3, 5)` — interp returned `(0, 0)`, expected `(1, 0)`; adding a `println` in the body flipped which backend was wrong.  **Closed (2026-05-11):** two compounding root causes both fixed.  **(a) Interp slot aliasing**: `src/variables/intervals.rs::compute_intervals` had no `Value::Tuple` arm — `Return(Tuple([Var(a), Var(b)]))` recursion fell through silently, the operand vars' last_use stayed at the default value, and the slot allocator considered them dead and aliased their slots.  When `a` and `b` were both written in the same scope, the second write clobbered the first; the tuple read returned `(b_value, b_value)`.  Fix: add `Value::Tuple(elems)`, `Value::TupleGet(_, _)`, and `Value::TuplePut(_, _, _)` arms that recurse into each element so reads update the operand vars' last_use correctly.  **(b) Native hoisted-return guard miss**: `scopes::free_vars` hoists the tuple value as a separate statement before the `OpFreeText(work)` cleanup, leaving `[Set(lt), Set(gt), Call(println), Tuple, OpFreeText, Return(Null)]`.  `src/generation/emit.rs::patch_hoisted_returns` already rewrites this to `Return(Tuple)` — but only when the block result type matches a small allow-list (Void / Never / `t_*` text-stub / `__ret_N` text temp).  T-stubs returning a tuple weren't in the list, so native emitted the tuple as a discarded statement and fell through to a hardcoded `return (0, 0)`.  Fix: add `is_t_stub_tuple_body` to the guard so tuple-returning T-stubs also run the patch.  Without (a) the no-side-effects shape was wrong on interp; without (b) the with-println shape was wrong on native.  Both shapes now correct on both backends. | 255 | **@P255** — Capturing the result of a generic-fn `vector` return into a local variable rejects with `"Variable X cannot change type from vector to vector"` — both sides of the diagnostic show the IDENTICAL type. Reproducer: `struct P { v: integer } fn make(x: T) -> vector { o: vector = []; o += [x]; o } fn main() { p = P{v:1}; vp = make(p); }` rejected on parse with the equal-types diagnostic; even a separate-line construction (`p = P{...}; vp = make(p);`) hit the same path. Surfaced 2026-05-11 during @P241 slice-3 regression test development. Independent of @P241 — the diagnostic fired before any IR rewrite or codegen ran. Initial diagnosis ("change_var Vector→Vector arm rejects identical types") was incomplete; investigation revealed THREE coordinated root causes, each of which had to be fixed for the struct-T pattern to work end-to-end. **Root cause 1 (the equal-types reject)**: when the call argument was a struct literal `P { v: 99 }` the expression's type carried `Type::Rewritten(Reference(P))` (the wrapper used to mark "rewritten into Insert ops"); that wrapper propagated into the bound T, then into `vector`, and `Type::is_equal` did not look through `Rewritten` so a `vector>>` LHS did not match a `vector>` RHS. **Root cause 2 (post-fix runtime garbage)**: stripping the wrapper in `is_equal` made the parse succeed but the runtime returned `4294967202` for `vp[0].v` instead of `99`. The `Rewritten(Reference(P))` was still flowing through `resolve_type_var` into the bound T, so `vector`'s element type was `Rewritten(Reference(P))` — codegen still mis-handled it. **Root cause 3 (parametric type-id inside OpCopyRecord)**: even with T cleanly bound to `Reference(P)`, the parametric template's vector-element-write triplet `OpNewRecord(out, t_T, …); OpCopyRecord(src, elm, t_T_known); OpFinishRecord(out, elm, t_T, …)` left the type-id args pointing at the parametric T's known_type after substitution. The runtime read the wrong record size from that placeholder type-id and returned garbage. @P241 slice 1-3 had only handled primitive T (replacing OpCopyRecord with OpSetXxx); struct T fell through with the parametric type-ids intact. **Closed (2026-05-12)** with three coordinated fixes: (a) `src/data.rs::Type::is_equal` strips `Type::Rewritten` wrappers on either side before unifying — Rewritten is a value-construction marker, not a shape difference. (b) `src/parser/mod.rs::resolve_type_var` strips `Rewritten` from the concrete arg type before binding T, so the marker (which describes how a particular arg was assembled, not the data shape T represents) never enters the substituted IR. (c) `src/parser/mod.rs::rewrite_vector_write_triplets` was extended to handle struct T (Reference): a new `is_rewritable_vector_element_target` predicate gates the rewrite on either primitive T OR struct T; for struct T the OpCopyRecord shape is kept but its `tp` arg is patched to the concrete struct's `known_type` (via `data.def(content_def_nr).known_type`) AND the surrounding OpNewRecord/OpFinishRecord `parent_tp` args get patched to `concrete_vec_tp` (already computed for the primitive path). PreAlloc prefix gets emitted for struct T too, matching the parse-time concrete-T path's perf parity. @P245.context: | 245 | **@P245** — `parallel { server_arm(...); client_arm(...); }` hangs indefinitely when one arm performs a blocking accept on a TCP listener and the other arm tries `web::ws_handler(...)` against the same loopback port.  Two compounding root causes, both fixed together (2026-05-10): **(a)** the worker thread's stack was empty when the arm body ran, so reads at the parent's frame offsets returned garbage — `port = 18092; parallel { server_arm(port); ... }` saw `port` arrive as 0 (or whatever stale bytes were at offset 8 in the worker's freshly-`database(1000)` record).  **(b)** `src/extensions.rs::native_auto_dispatch` held the `NATIVE_SIGS` mutex guard ACROSS the native-fn invocation — when a sibling worker called a blocking native fn (`n_tcp_accept`'s `listener.accept()`), the guard stayed held; every other worker calling any auto-marshalled native fn (`web::sleep_ms`, `web::ws_handler`, etc.) blocked on `NATIVE_SIGS.lock()` indefinitely.  This serialised every parallel arm whenever one arm did blocking I/O, manifesting as the original "client thread silently never starts" symptom.  **Closed (2026-05-10)** with two coordinated changes: (1) `src/state/mod.rs::parallel_join` captures the parent's stack contents (offsets 4..stack_pos) into an `Arc<Vec<u8>>` snapshot, threaded through `run_parallel_block` to each worker; the new `State::execute_at_void_with_snapshot` overlays the snapshot on the worker's stack at offset 4 and sets `stack_pos` to mirror the parent's, so variable reads at parent-frame offsets resolve correctly.  Arms still get isolated `Stores` clones via `clone_for_worker`, so writes inside an arm don't propagate back.  (2) `src/extensions.rs::native_auto_dispatch` now clones the `(sym, sig)` entry out of the `NATIVE_SIGS` table and DROPS the mutex guard before `dispatch_call` — the lock is held only for the table lookup, never for the call. | 254 | **@P254** — **Security — local cache poisoning.**  `loft --native script.loft` checks `.loft/cache/<source_stem>-<source_hash>` (`src/main.rs:2286`) and, if the file existed, executed it directly via `Command::new(&binary)` (`src/main.rs:2485`) without verifying that loft itself produced it.  The filename is content-addressed (`<u64 hash>` of source bytes + `--native-release`/`--native-debug` flags + `libloft.rlib` mtime + per-package native rlib mtimes) so an attacker who knows the source AND the host's libloft.rlib mtime can pre-compute the cache filename and drop a malicious ELF there.  Pre-fix the cache directory at `<source_dir>/.loft/cache/` was created with default mode (typically `775` — group-writable on most umasks); cached binaries were mode `755` (executable).  No HMAC, no signature, no owner check at execute time.  **Threat scenarios** (low severity — local file access required): shared dev machine where a colleague drops a poisoned cache before you run; cloned project that ships a `.loft/cache/` directory unintentionally (the dir lives next to source so it travels via `git clone` unless `.gitignore`d); CI cache volumes restored from a previous job's artifact when another tenant could write to the artifact storage.  Same shape as the well-known `ccache` / `sccache` / Bazel-remote-cache poisoning class.  Surfaced 2026-05-11 during a security audit prompted by the user pointing at the hash-DoS (@P253).  **Closed (2026-05-12)** with three coordinated defenses chosen from the cheapest-first list (HMAC+secret avoided — adds crypto dependency without strengthening the threat model materially; the simpler defenses cover the documented attack scenarios): (a) `cache_safe_to_execute` in `src/native_utils.rs` rejects any cached binary that is a symlink (all platforms), or that is owned by another uid, group/other-readable/writable, or carries SUID/SGID bits (Unix); the cache lookup site in `src/main.rs:2286` uses this check to decide whether to reuse the cache or recompile.  (b) `tighten_cache_dir` + `tighten_cache_binary` `chmod 0o700` the directory and freshly written binary on Unix, repairing pre-existing wider-mode caches from earlier loft versions.  (c) `LOFT_NATIVE_NO_CACHE=1` opts out of the cache entirely — bypasses lookup AND skips writing — for paranoid users who want zero on-disk artifacts.  When the safety check rejects a cached binary, loft prints `"rejecting suspicious cached binary at <path> (P254 — wrong owner, world-writable, symlink, or SUID); recompiling"` to stderr and recompiles instead of refusing service.  Cache writes that can't tighten the directory mode (e.g. NFS server-enforced mode) skip the cache write entirely with a one-line warning.  Pinned by `tests/p254_cache_poisoning.rs` (5 integration cells: fresh-cache permissions, second-run reuse, group-writable rejected, drop-poisoned-binary-not-executed, `LOFT_NATIVE_NO_CACHE=1` skips writes) + `src/native_utils.rs::p254_cache_safety` (5 unit cells covering each rejection axis). | 283 | **@P283** — Format-string interpolation of a self-slice-reassigned text PARAMETER crashes both backends.  Pattern that triggers it:  (1) fn with 2+ text parameters; (2) self-slice reassignment of one param (`rb = rb[plen..olen];`); (3) format-string return that interpolates BOTH the reassigned param (`{rb}`) AND another param (`{id}`) — `"[{id}] {rb}"`.  Interpreter SIGSEGV'd at op=116 (`OpAppendText`); native failed to compile with rustc E0368 (`var___work_2 += &*(...)` where `var___work_2` is `&mut String`).  **Closed (2026-05-18)** in @PLAN37 phase 10.10b.  Root cause: the parser's `assign_text` work-text path (`src/parser/operators.rs:106-113`) constructs `Value::Call(OpAppendText, …)` / `OpClearText` / `OpFormatText` IR for self-referencing text assignments inside a text-returning function.  `text_return` (`src/parser/control.rs:2919`) then promotes the work-text local to a `RefVar(Text)` hidden argument so the buffer is passed in by reference.  But the operator-call codegen path on BOTH backends emitted the local-String variant of these ops — interpreter's `append_text` (`src/state/text.rs:78`) called `string_mut` on what was actually a refvar DbRef slot (treating its 12 bytes as `String` → SIGSEGV); native's `append_text` (`src/generation/text.rs:139`) emitted `var += &*(…)` on a `&mut String` (E0368).  Fix mirrored the existing B7 dispatch (`OpAppendCharacter` → `OpAppendStackCharacter` for RefVar targets) to cover the full op cluster: when the first arg is `Value::Var(v)` with `Type::RefVar(Type::Text(_))`, rewrite to the Stack variant.  Added in `src/state/codegen.rs::generate_call` (bytecode emit — interp dispatch) AND `src/generation/dispatch.rs::output_call_inner` (native emit dispatch).  Op set: `OpAppendText` → `OpAppendStackText`, `OpClearText` → `OpClearStackText`, `OpAppendCharacter` → `OpAppendStackCharacter`, `OpFormatText` → `OpFormatStackText`, `OpFormatInt` → `OpFormatStackInt`, `OpFormatFloat` → `OpFormatStackFloat`, `OpFormatSingle` → `OpFormatStackSingle`, `OpFormatDatabase` → `OpFormatStackDatabase`.  Native side ALSO needed a `refvar_text_clone` arm in `output_set` (`src/generation/dispatch.rs:319`) for the `OpSet(local_String, Var(refvar_text_arg))` shape — `output_code_inner` emits `&*var_X` for RefVar(Text) Var reads (`src/generation/emit.rs:141`); appending `.to_string()` parses as `&*(var_X.to_string())` per Rust precedence → `&str` not `String` → E0308.  Fix: emit `var_X.to_string()` directly (auto-deref through `&mut String` produces an owned String of the right type). Emit `var_X.to_string()` directly instead.  Pinned by `tests/scripts/111-format-string-self-slice.loft`.  Actual effort: ~2 h (vs M 4-8 h estimate). |

@P319.context: | 319 | **@P319** — **FIXED 2026-05-23** — INTERPRETER-ONLY (native was always correct): a lambda stored in a local that CAPTURES a struct and APPENDS a nested-constructed element to the captured struct's `vector<…>` field corrupted the captured struct on the SECOND invocation.  Surfaced at `lib/moros_render/tests/adversarial.loft` (`m_adv3.vertices += [vertex(vec3(x,y,z), up_adv, uv_adv)]` inside a captured lambda → SIGSEGV op=196 `new_record`).  Offset-0 vector field → silent data-loss (`len` stuck at 0: 1st append `inside len=1`, 2nd `inside len=0`); non-zero-offset field → SIGSEGV.  **TRUE ROOT CAUSE** (the earlier "(`copy_claims`/`record_new` store-recycle)" hypothesis was DISPROVEN — `copy_claims` is clean for inline-nested structs, and the same nested append INLINE works): the **void-return closure write-back** (`src/parser/control.rs`, the post-call capture reload) emitted `outer = OpGetDbRef(closure, off)` for EVERY capture — including shared-reference captures stored via the auto-Reference 12-byte DbRef encoding (closure attribute `Reference(d, deps)`, non-empty deps).  For these the interpreter's ref-reassignment freed the OLD store BEFORE writing the SAME DbRef back over itself (`FreeRef(old m)` then `GetDbRef`): a premature free of a store the closure record still referenced (`m`'s `ref_count` is 1 — captured structs got NO `OpIncRc`, unlike boxed `__cell_*` scalars).  The next invocation reused the freed store for its temps, clobbering the captured struct.  Native compiles the same IR without that free, so only the interpreter corrupted.  **FIX:** generalise the write-back skip (previously `__cell_*`-only) to ALL shared-reference captures (`matches!(attr_type, Type::Reference(_, deps) if !deps.is_empty())`) — the closure already shares the live store, so the reload was redundant as well as harmful. Two attempted fixes during the session went in the WRONG direction — both routed `n_load_png` / `n_save_png` through `src/codegen_runtime.rs` (mirroring the @P321a crypto pattern), adding library Rust code into the loft compiler crate.  **User correction (2026-05-23):** the project goal is the REVERSE — get library code OUT of the compiler crate, not add more in.  `src/native.rs` already carries 19 hand-maintained library `n_*` entries (`n_sha256` and 18 others); the crypto block in `src/codegen_runtime.rs` is the same anti-pattern.  Plan `lib_plans/12-library-extraction` (promoted from `future/` to active 2026-05-23) is the correct vehicle — Phase 1 drains `src/native.rs` of library symbols, then `lib/imaging/native/` moves to a real external crate consumable via the package registry.  @P321c stays open until the imaging library's `n_load_png` resolves via the package's own native crate (no compiler-crate routing).  Direct-call ABI gap (lack of struct-ref marshalling) is a real native-codegen limitation but its fix lives downstream of the extraction work, not in the compiler crate.  **@P321d `moros_map/serial` — FIXED 2026-05-23**: nested vector index `m.a[0].b[2]` emitted two live `&mut stores` borrows (E0499).  `vec_get_or_raise_runtime` is a `&mut self` method (it may `raise_runtime` on OOB); the outer `stores.vec_get_or_raise_runtime(&<inner>, …)` holds its receiver borrow across argument evaluation, and `<inner>` expands to another `vec_get_or_raise_runtime` → second `&mut stores`.  Fix: the `OpGetVector` / `OpVectorRef` `#rust` templates (`default/01_code.loft`) now bind `@r` to a local first — `{{let __vr = @r; s.vec_get_or_raise(&__vr, …)}}` — fully evaluating the inner borrow (owned `DbRef`) before the outer call.  `src/fill.rs` regenerated (`make fill`); the interpreter gets the same harmless local binding.  Regression `tests/scripts/repro_p321d.loft` (both backends).  **@P321e `moros_editor` — FIXED 2026-05-23**: a text-returning fn whose body is a `match` of format strings `.to_string()`'d the match result into a `__ret_N` LOCAL `String`, then returned `Str::new(&local)` — a borrow of a fn-local that drops at return (runtime `ptr::copy` panic on the caller's `.to_string()`).  A RefVar work-buffer arg existed but the fn returned a DIFFERENT local, so the P205 scratch guard didn't fire.  Fix (`src/generation/emit.rs`): the text-Return also routes through `stores.scratch` when the returned value is a text LOCAL var.  moros_editor 5/5 files native + interp.  **@P321f `random` — FIXED 2026-05-23**: two native bugs — (1) `rand_seed` (`#native "n_rand_seed"`, void) fell through to an EMPTY stub (P269 only errors for non-void) → silent no-op → reproducible-seed asserts failed; wired `n_rand_seed` into `CODEGEN_RUNTIME_FNS` + `codegen_runtime::n_rand_seed` (delegates to `cr_rand_seed`).  (2) `n_rand_indices` stored 4-byte i32 elements but `vector<integer>` is read with 8-byte (i64) stride → index pairs merged ("missing value N"); now stores i64.  native + interp 11/11.  **@P321g `moros_ui` — FIXED 2026-05-23**: a `&`-ref-param call on an assignment RHS (`ec_hit = route_click(p, st.es_tools, …)`) emitted a `let` in expression position → `error: expected expression, found 'let' statement`.  The `&`-ref arg `st.es_tools` (an addressable field) materialises a `Set(__ref_N, OpGetField…)` statement ahead of the call, so the RHS is `Insert([Set(__ref_N, …), Call])` — wrapped in `Value::Span` for source-position tracking.  `output_set`'s S35 hoist (`src/generation/dispatch.rs`) — which exists to lift all-but-last Insert ops to statements — matched only a *bare* `Insert`, so `Span(Insert)` fell through to the brace-less `Insert` arm of `output_code_inner`, producing `let x = let __ref_N = …; call()`.  Fix: S35 unspans `to` before the check.  moros_ui 4/4 files native + interp. Full design in [STDLIB.md § Canonical object serialization](STDLIB.md#canonical-object-serialization-planned--see-p289).  Today: `f += text` and `f += vector<T>` write raw bytes with no length prefix (callers must track size out-of-band), `f += plain_struct` writes internal storage handle bytes (NOT field values), and `f#read as MyStruct` is unimplemented — users read each scalar field individually and rebuild the struct in user code.  End state: length-prefixed text / vectors + per-field struct serialization for both directions, so `f += my_struct` ↔ `s = f#read as MyStruct` round-trips arbitrary loft objects.  Infrastructure mostly there: `OpReadFile` (`src/state/io.rs::read_file`) already accepts an arbitrary `db_tp` + the inferred-size path in `src/parser/objects.rs` already routes through the canonical `sizeof` resolver.  Missing: (a) prefix-length convention for text / vectors (new wire-format flag or struct shape), (b) `dispatch_read_data` extension to walk struct field layout, (c) reject collection-bearing structs in the legacy unprefixed path with a clear diagnostic.  Symmetric inverse `f#read(N) as vector<T>` (N elements known at read site) is the simpler half — useful right away for GLB-style chunk-size-in-header formats.  Surfaced 2026-05-19 in `lib/world/world_load` and `tools/audience-demo/single_port_server.loft::world_load`. Pre-fix the cache directory at `<source_dir>/.loft/cache/` was created with default mode (typically `775` — group-writable on most umasks); cached binaries were mode `755` (executable).  No HMAC, no signature, no owner check at execute time.  **Threat scenarios** (low severity — local file access required): shared dev machine where a colleague drops a poisoned cache before you run; cloned project that ships a `.loft/cache/` directory unintentionally (the dir lives next to source so it travels via `git clone` unless `.gitignore`d); CI cache volumes restored from a previous job's artifact when another tenant could write to the artifact storage. | **P5** — `vector +=` capacity reservation (amortised growth) | — | — | Interpreter + Native | **LANDED 2026-05-21.**  Discovered via the `store_memory()` builtin while profiling the @PLAN36 crystal mesh: single-element `+= [x]` reallocated the backing record on (nearly) every append, fragmenting the store into O(N) freed records (a 12 738-element build → **101 815 free blocks / ~250 MB** vs ~0.8 MB of data).  Fixed by amortised (~×2) growth in `vector::vector_append` (`src/vector.rs`): when the backing record is out of room it grows to ~2× `length+1` instead of exactly `length+1`; `Store::resize` is grow-only so in-room appends are no-ops.  Length lives in a separate field (word 1), so the trailing slack never affects `len()`/indexing/copy (length-based, shrinks to fit)/serialisation.  One shared function → both backends.  Same 12 000-element build now shows **~8 free blocks** (one trailing slack block).  Guards: `tests/scripts/124-vector-amortised-growth.loft` (cross-mode correctness + fragmentation digit-count bound).  `vector_set_size` (bulk `+= [a,b,c]`) and `insert_vector` keep exact sizing (not the hot path); a user-facing `reserve(v, n)` (wrapping the existing `OpPreAllocVector`) remains an optional opt-in follow-up. |

| **P6** — Free-block coalescing in `Store` (merge mergeable neighbours) | — | — | Interpreter + Native | **LANDED 2026-05-21.**  Partner of P5.  `Store::delete` coalesces only FORWARD (`rec + size`) — the header-only block layout has no footer, so a freed block can't find its PREDECESSOR; freeing B while A is already free left A|B uncoalesced, and accumulated small free blocks forced the store to GROW instead of reusing freed space.  **Fixed with NO new index** (no end→start map, no boundary-tag footer — those grow with the free-block count): a lazy `coalesce_free` sweep walks the contiguous block chain (the adjacency info that already exists — the same walk `claim_scan`/`usage`/`fl_rebuild` do), merges every run of adjacent free blocks in place, and rebuilds the ONE existing size-keyed free tree via `fl_rebuild`.  It runs in `claim` only when a best-fit miss would otherwise grow the store (that path already costs O(n) via `resize_store`), guarded by a single `needs_coalesce` bool so alloc-only workloads never sweep.  Backward coalescing falls out of the address-order walk (A+B merge regardless of free order).  Shared `Store` → both backends.  Guards: Rust unit test `coalesce_free_merges_adjacent_and_reuses_space` (`src/store.rs` — mergeable-pairs → 0, merged block reused without growing), cross-mode `tests/scripts/126-store-coalesce.loft`. |

legacy:plan-16.context: | 327 | **@P327** — **FIXED 2026-05-23 (both backends).**  Two bugs, same family.  (1) **Interp** silently skipped the for-loop body when iterating a tuple-yielding generator (`count=0` instead of running per-yield).  Root: the for-loop's break check at `parser/collections.rs::iter_for` ran `OpNot(test_for)` after a failed `convert(Tuple, Boolean)`, so `OpNot` read one byte of the 16-byte tuple as boolean — non-deterministic termination.  Fix: emit `OpCoroutineExhausted(__gen_N)` instead.  (2) **Native** failed to compile — tuple yields (16 bytes) collided with text (`&str` = 16) in the `OpCoroutineNext` channel dispatch.  Adding one hardcoded channel per tuple shape (`next_tuple_2i64`, `next_tuple_3i64`, …) would have reproduced the @PLAN15 closure combinatorial trap.  Instead: introduced the **unified `next_into(stores, &mut [i64])` channel** (plan-16 phase 01) — one trait method that every yield shape can use by encoding its own layout in slot writes.  `value_size` now packs (low byte = byte size, high byte = channel tag); the interp masks the tag off (`fill.rs` + `state/codegen.rs::OpCoroutineNext` arm — the latter was the slot-allocator regression that an earlier attempt missed), the native dispatch reads both bytes and emits a stack `[i64; N]` buffer + tuple rebuild.  Both manual `next()` (`control.rs`) and the for-loop driver (`collections.rs`) use the same encoding.  Regression: 4 tests in `tests/issues.rs::p327_*` + matrix cells `y4_x1_tuple_for_loop` + `y4_x2_tuple_manual_next` (16/16 matrix cells green). | 289 | **@P289** — Canonical object serialization for binary files is not implemented.  Full design in [STDLIB.md § Canonical object serialization](STDLIB.md#canonical-object-serialization-planned--see-p289).  Today: `f += text` and `f += vector<T>` write raw bytes with no length prefix (callers must track size out-of-band), `f += plain_struct` writes internal storage handle bytes (NOT field values), and `f#read as MyStruct` is unimplemented — users read each scalar field individually and rebuild the struct in user code.  End state: length-prefixed text / vectors + per-field struct serialization for both directions, so `f += my_struct` ↔ `s = f#read as MyStruct` round-trips arbitrary loft objects.  Infrastructure mostly there: `OpReadFile` (`src/state/io.rs::read_file`) already accepts an arbitrary `db_tp` + the inferred-size path in `src/parser/objects.rs` already routes through the canonical `sizeof` resolver.  Missing: (a) prefix-length convention for text / vectors (new wire-format flag or struct shape), (b) `dispatch_read_data` extension to walk struct field layout, (c) reject collection-bearing structs in the legacy unprefixed path with a clear diagnostic.  Symmetric inverse `f#read(N) as vector<T>` (N elements known at read site) is the simpler half — useful right away for GLB-style chunk-size-in-header formats.  Surfaced 2026-05-19 in `lib/world/world_load` and `tools/audience-demo/single_port_server.loft::world_load`.  Likely fix sites: `src/parser/objects.rs::has_keyword("read")` + `src/state/io.rs::dispatch_read_data` + new write path in the `f += value` codegen (`src/parser/expressions.rs::append_to_file`).  **Append-semantics fix landed 2026-05-20** (separate from the canonical-serialization work): `f += value` now APPENDS to the end of the file — re-opening a file and writing preserves earlier bytes — matching `vector += [elem]` and `text += "more"`.  Implemented by switching `src/state/io.rs::write_file` (interp) + `src/codegen_runtime.rs::{OpWriteFile, file_handle_write}` (native) from `File::create` (truncate) to `OpenOptions … .truncate(false)` with the default write position seeking to file size; explicit `f#next = N` still overwrites in place.  Companion op `file.sync()` (`OpSyncFile` → `File::sync_data()`) flushes buffered bytes so log records / blocks are durable before the next write.  **Migration**: code that relied on `+=` truncating on first re-open must now call `f.set_file_size(0)` (or `f#size = 0`) before the first write — updated call sites: `single_port_server.loft::world_save`, `lib/world/src/world.loft::world_save`, `lib/graphics/src/glb.loft`, `scripts/build-playground-examples.loft`.  Regression tests: `tests/scripts/114-file-sync.loft`, `115-snapshot-roundtrip.loft`, `116-file-append-log.loft`.  **Moved 2026-05-20 to [@PLAN43 — Binary file I/O type matrix](plans/future/43-binary-io-validation/README.md)**: the remaining canonical-serialization work (length-prefixed text/vectors, per-field struct serialization, `f#read as MyStruct`) is now the design half of that validation plan, where it gets a value-type × format × access-pattern round-trip matrix on both backends.  Kept here as a workaround reference until the plan ships. | Moved to @PLAN43 | Read each field individually: `c_color = f#read as u8; c_height = f#read as u8; c_age = f#read as u16; cell = Cell{c_color: c_color, c_height: c_height, c_age: c_age}` (lib/world's `world_load` pattern).  For vectors: emit a length prefix manually and read N times in a `while` loop.  For repeated writes to the same path, call `f.set_file_size(0)` first (now that `+=` appends). |

A removed cell simply disappears; an alpha fade-out on the `4:x,y,0` delta (shipped 2026-05-20, ~600 ms, no wire change) is the lightweight cosmetic substitute — in the **browser client** (`doc/audience-demo/index.html`, an rAF-driven alpha ramp) AND the **native projector** (`projector.loft`, which unified its cell shader on per-vertex RGBA + `GL_BLEND` and re-emits the erased cell's ground footprint at dwindling alpha).  This removes the shrink animation as a driver for age-on-wire.  `DECAY_WINDOW` now just adds a flat tail to total lifetime.  **1.8 multi-client load test shipped** (2026-05-20): [`tools/audience-demo/load_test.loft`](../../../../tools/audience-demo/load_test.loft) — one driver process opens N real WS connections, paints disjoint cells, drains the broadcast fan-out, and reports per-tier metrics; ramps 3 → 12 → 30 clients by default (`LOFT_AUD_CLIENTS` for a single tier).  **Findings** (3/12/30 clients × 10 paints, fresh world, interp): broadcast correctness is solid — **100% fan-out, 0 send failures, 0 drops at every tier** (every paint reached every client).  **The bottleneck is connection establishment, not throughput**: per-client connect latency degrades super-linearly (0.6 → 2.8 → 7.3 s/client), so all 30 clients took **~220 s** to connect.  **Root cause (corrected after a Tier-A prototype):** it is **not** the loft loop — a loft-level Tier A (incremental replay + batched accept + snapshot deferral, all shipped in `single_port_server.loft` as sound concurrency hygiene) was prototyped and **did not move connect latency** (210 s vs 220 s).  A TCP-layer experiment (2026-05-20) pinned the exact cause: WS streams accepted via the manual HTTP-upgrade path keep a **500 ms read timeout** that `n_ws_upgrade` never resets, so every idle-client poll blocks 500 ms → `connect[k] ≈ k × 505 ms` → O(N²).  `TCP_NODELAY` made no difference, and lowering the timeout / peek-gating broke `multiplayer_v3` (lossy `read_exact` framing).  **The real fix was that `lib/server` already had a safe path** — the event pump (`srv.run`/`n_ws_next_event`, 20 ms streams, `NoData`-aware `ws_read_frame_detailed`), the supported multi-client path validated by TTT v5.  **A′ (shipped 2026-05-20)** taught the pump to also serve plain HTTP (new `AcceptOutcome::Http` + `Server::poll_event` / `respond_*`) and rewrote the audience server onto it (clients keyed by `cid`, fan-out via `srv.broadcast`).  **Result: 30-client connect 220 s → ~10 s (21.6×), 100 % fan-out, page still served, `multiplayer_v2/v3/v5` green.**  See [§ Tier A′](01-server-state.md).  True O(ready) scaling (epoll, idle clients cost zero) is still Tier B.  **1.9 crash-resistance shipped** (2026-05-20): audited the pump path against hostile clients — found + fixed an unbounded WS-frame allocation (`payload_len` claiming ~u64::MAX → process abort; now capped at 16 MiB, regression test `p_oversized_ws_frame_rejected_without_alloc`); malformed text frames + dropped handshakes already survive (probed via [`crash_probe.loft`](../../../../tools/audience-demo/crash_probe.loft)).  **All of sub-arc 1 (server) is now done.**  Wire is `<msg_id>:<payload>` (MVP); spec'd migration to JSON-in / binary-out is filed as phase 1 step 2.  **WsGroup shipped** (2026-05-20): multiplexed non-blocking client receiver in `lib/web` — load test send phase dropped from ~295 s to 19 ms for 30 clients; server validated live for ~4 hours (18:04–22:00 Amsterdam, zero crashes) |

| 289 | **@P289** — Canonical object serialization for binary files is not implemented.  Full design in [STDLIB.md § Canonical object serialization](STDLIB.md#canonical-object-serialization-planned--see-p289).  Today: `f += text` and `f += vector<T>` write raw bytes with no length prefix (callers must track size out-of-band), `f += plain_struct` writes internal storage handle bytes (NOT field values), and `f#read as MyStruct` is unimplemented — users read each scalar field individually and rebuild the struct in user code.  End state: length-prefixed text / vectors + per-field struct serialization for both directions, so `f += my_struct` ↔ `s = f#read as MyStruct` round-trips arbitrary loft objects.  Infrastructure mostly there: `OpReadFile` (`src/state/io.rs::read_file`) already accepts an arbitrary `db_tp` + the inferred-size path in `src/parser/objects.rs` already routes through the canonical `sizeof` resolver.  Missing: (a) prefix-length convention for text / vectors (new wire-format flag or struct shape), (b) `dispatch_read_data` extension to walk struct field layout, (c) reject collection-bearing structs in the legacy unprefixed path with a clear diagnostic.  Symmetric inverse `f#read(N) as vector<T>` (N elements known at read site) is the simpler half — useful right away for GLB-style chunk-size-in-header formats.  Surfaced 2026-05-19 in `lib/world/world_load` and `tools/audience-demo/single_port_server.loft::world_load`.  Likely fix sites: `src/parser/objects.rs::has_keyword("read")` + `src/state/io.rs::dispatch_read_data` + new write path in the `f += value` codegen (`src/parser/expressions.rs::append_to_file`).  **Append-semantics fix landed 2026-05-20** (separate from the canonical-serialization work): `f += value` now APPENDS to the end of the file — re-opening a file and writing preserves earlier bytes — matching `vector += [elem]` and `text += "more"`.  Implemented by switching `src/state/io.rs::write_file` (interp) + `src/codegen_runtime.rs::{OpWriteFile, file_handle_write}` (native) from `File::create` (truncate) to `OpenOptions … .truncate(false)` with the default write position seeking to file size; explicit `f#next = N` still overwrites in place.  Companion op `file.sync()` (`OpSyncFile` → `File::sync_data()`) flushes buffered bytes so log records / blocks are durable before the next write.  **Migration**: code that relied on `+=` truncating on first re-open must now call `f.set_file_size(0)` (or `f#size = 0`) before the first write — updated call sites: `single_port_server.loft::world_save`, `lib/world/src/world.loft::world_save`, `lib/graphics/src/glb.loft`, `scripts/build-playground-examples.loft`.  Regression tests: `tests/scripts/114-file-sync.loft`, `115-snapshot-roundtrip.loft`, `116-file-append-log.loft`.  **Moved 2026-05-20 to [@PLAN43 — Binary file I/O type matrix](plans/future/43-binary-io-validation/README.md)**: the remaining canonical-serialization work (length-prefixed text/vectors, per-field struct serialization, `f#read as MyStruct`) is now the design half of that validation plan, where it gets a value-type × format × access-pattern round-trip matrix on both backends.  Kept here as a workaround reference until the plan ships. | Moved to @PLAN43 | Read each field individually: `c_color = f#read as u8; c_height = f#read as u8; c_age = f#read as u16; cell = Cell{c_color: c_color, c_height: c_height, c_age: c_age}` (lib/world's `world_load` pattern).  For vectors: emit a length prefix manually and read N times in a `while` loop.  For repeated writes to the same path, call `f.set_file_size(0)` first (now that `+=` appends). |
